newsitem.title: ROMANIA: BUCHAREST EQUITIES UP, BOURSE INDICES AT YEAR HIGH.
newsitem.headline: BUCHAREST EQUITIES UP, BOURSE INDICES AT YEAR HIGH.

text.p: Buying pressure sent most
share prices up on Thursday on the Bucharest bourse and among
the most attractive over-the-counter shares.
The bourse saw two independent market indices hit year
highs and traders forecast continued high demand.
On the OTC market, a bullish market was also predicted on
the back of a decision this week by the centirst coalition
government to take conttrol of Romania's main privatisation
agency. "This step is expected to step up the full
privatisation of the OTC-listed companies," a trader said.
The Bourse's VAB and BIG indices rose by 3.7 and 3.9
percent respectively from the previous session to 568.6 and
578.14 points. The BIG first-tier index climbed by 5.29 percent
to 1,883.54 points.
Traders said a drop in bourse turnover to 3.2 billion lei
from Wednesday's 4.0 billion was a result of a smaller number
of accumulated orders in the market.
Three high-caps and another 10 stocks on the second tier
drifted higher, seven stocks fell, six remained unchanged and
one had no trade. Five companies remained suspended pending
release of details on their stockholders' meeting.
An independent index for the OTC market computed by
Bucharest Investment Group brokerage house climbed by 8.8
percent to 1758.01 points, mostly on the strength of rises in
the prices of cement makers Romcim, Casial and Moldocim.
The Bourse's main performers were Azomures
fertiliser which closed slighly stronger at 1,880 lei and
Chemical plant Oltchim , 20 lei higher at 1,370.
The first-tier's biggest gainer, though with lower volumes,
was Antibiotice pharmaceuticals company, which firmed
to 4,000 lei, 500 up on the previous level.
"Existing Antibiotice supply could not meet the mounting
demand for the stock," said a broker, adding that he saw
further rises ahead for the Antibiotice price.
In OTC trading, Casial had the day's highest volume of
681,712 shares, closing 175 lei firmer at 1,175. Romcim gained
2,000 lei to 53,000, while Moldocim was 5,000 lei up at 34,000.
Volumes on the RASDAQ rose to 3.4 million shares from
around 3.0 million on Wednesday, but the turnover fell to 6.04
billion lei from over 7.0 billion previously. The system, which
lists 2,719 companies, traded 467 stocks on Thursday.
